p.src: Intuition Built for the Wrong World

u.src: Intuition Built for the Wrong World
en: Intuition Built for the Wrong World
ja: 誤った世界のために築かれた直観
zh: 为错误世界建立的直觉

p.src: Our physical intuition is old. Long before anyone wrote an equation, an animal chasing prey had to estimate relative speed and direction. If a lion is gaining on an antelope, the lion is responding to a changing separation and therefore, in an implicit way, to relative velocity. Nervous systems that handled such judgments well were favored; those that handled them badly did not leave many descendants. Much of what we call common sense about motion was trained in this ordinary world.

ja: 我々の物理的直観は古い。誰かが方程式を書くはるか以前から、獲物を追う動物は相対的な速さと方向を見積もらねばならなかった。ライオンがレイヨウに追いつきつつあるなら、ライオンは変化する間隔に反応しており、したがって暗黙のうちに相対速度に反応している。そのような判断をうまく扱う神経系が選ばれ、それをうまく扱えないものは多くの子孫を残さなかった。運動について我々が常識と呼ぶものの多くは、この日常世界で鍛えられたのである。
zh: 我们的物理直觉由来已久。早在任何人写下方程之前，追逐猎物的动物就必须估计相对速度和方向。如果一头狮子正在逼近一只羚羊，狮子是在对不断变化的间距作出反应，因此是以一种隐含的方式对相对速度作出反应。能够很好地处理这类判断的神经系统受到了青睐；处理得差的那些没有留下多少后代。我们关于运动的所谓常识，大多是在这个平凡世界中训练出来的。

p.src: That inheritance is useful, but narrow. Nothing in ordinary life moves close to the speed of light, so evolution supplied no instinct for relativistic spacetime. A physicist first learns the abstract geometry and only later acquires a new intuition for it. Quantum mechanics is harder still. Our familiar picture of a particle comes from rocks and arrows: at each instant the object has a position, the succession of positions forms a trajectory, and changes of position define a velocity. An electron does not oblige us by fitting that picture. Position uncertainty and the absence of a classical trajectory have no analogue in the experience that shaped our senses.

ja: その遺産は有用だが、狭い。日常生活では何も光速に近い速さで動かないため、進化は相対論的時空に対する本能を与えなかった。物理学者はまず抽象的な幾何学を学び、その後になって初めてそれに対する新しい直観を獲得する。量子力学はさらに難しい。我々がよく知る粒子の像は石や矢から来ている。すなわち、各瞬間に物体は位置を持ち、位置の連なりが軌道をなし、位置の変化が速度を定義する。電子はその像に都合よく当てはまってはくれない。位置の不確定性と古典的軌道の不在は、我々の感覚を形作った経験の中に対応物を持たない。
zh: 这份遗产很有用，但很狭窄。日常生活中没有任何东西以接近光速运动，因此进化没有提供关于相对论时空的本能。物理学家先学习抽象几何，之后才获得对它的新直觉。量子力学还要更难。我们熟悉的粒子图景来自石头和箭：在每一瞬间物体都有一个位置，位置的相继形成一条轨迹，位置的变化定义速度。电子并不迁就我们去符合那幅图景。位置不确定性和经典轨迹的缺失，在塑造我们感官的经验中没有对应物。

p.src: There is no paradox in this failure of intuition. There would be a paradox only if instincts adapted to stones, animals, and modest speeds somehow knew in advance about electrons. The right response is to build a different intuition from a small set of precise rules. Here the emphasis will not be the usual route through wave mechanics and the Schrödinger equation. We will concentrate on the logical structure of quantum mechanics and on quantum information. Before asking what a quantum bit is, we must understand exactly what an ordinary bit does.

zh: 这种直觉的失败并不存在悖论。只有当适应石头、动物和中等速度的本能不知何故预先了解电子时，才会存在悖论。正确的回应是从一小组精确规则出发建立一种不同的直觉。这里的重点不会是通常经由波动力学和Schrödinger方程的路线。我们将集中关注量子力学的逻辑结构和量子信息。在追问量子比特是什么之前，我们必须确切理解普通比特做什么。

p.src: Encoding an Apparently Continuous World

u.src: Encoding an Apparently Continuous World
en: Encoding an Apparently Continuous World
ja: 一見連続に見える世界の符号化
zh: 编码一个看似连续的世界

p.src: Bits are not confined to coins. Any measured quantity known to finite accuracy can be written as a finite binary string. Suppose, for example, that the temperature of a room is required only to a chosen number of significant figures. Express the measured value in base two and retain the digits needed for that accuracy. Greater precision requires a longer string, but no change of principle.

Suppose, for example, that the temperature of a room is required only to a chosen number of significant figures. Express the measured value in base two and retain the digits needed for that accuracy. Greater precision requires a longer string, but no change of principle.
en: Bits are not confined to coins. Any measured quantity known to finite accuracy can be written as a finite binary string. Suppose, for example, that the temperature of a room is required only to a chosen number of significant figures. Express the measured value in base two and retain the digits needed for that accuracy. Greater precision requires a longer string, but no change of principle.
ja: ビットはコインに限られない。有限の精度で知られている任意の測定値は、有限の二進文字列として書くことができる。例えば、部屋の温度が選んだ有効数字の桁数までしか要求されないとしよう。測定値を二進法で表し、その精度に必要な桁を保持する。より高い精度にはより長い文字列が必要だが、原理の変更はない。
zh: 比特并不局限于硬币。任何已知到有限精度的被测量量都可以写成一个有限二进制串。例如，假设一个房间的温度只要求达到选定的有效数字位数。把测得的值用二进制表示，并保留达到该精度所需的数字。更高的精度需要更长的串，但原理不变。

p.src: A spatially varying field can be treated similarly. Divide the room into a fine ordered lattice of cells, record the field value in each cell to finite precision, and concatenate the resulting binary strings. Making the cells smaller improves spatial resolution; keeping more binary digits improves the field-value resolution. Temperature fields, electric fields, and magnetic fields can all be encoded this way to any prescribed finite accuracy.

Making the cells smaller improves spatial resolution; keeping more binary digits improves the field-value resolution. Temperature fields, electric fields, and magnetic fields can all be encoded this way to any prescribed finite accuracy.

p.src: The construction explains why digital computers can simulate physics. A computer stores finite strings, while finite resolution turns measured quantities and fields into precisely such strings. The approximation can be improved systematically by refining the lattice, the time step, or the number of retained digits.

p.src: Response: An exact real number may require infinitely many bits. Some rational binary expansions repeat, and a generic irrational expansion never terminates. A real computer always keeps finitely many digits. The point is that any specified finite accuracy can be encoded, not that every classical real number has a finite exact description.

Let $B=(B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4)$ be a row with the same number of entries as the column $A$. Their product is defined by matching positions and summing: $\begin{aligned}BA
  &=
  (B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4)
  \begin{pmatrix}
    A_1\\ A_2\\ A_3\\ A_4
  \end{pmatrix}\\
  &=B_1A_1+B_2A_2+B_3A_3+B_4A_4.
  \end{aligned}$ The result is a number, not another vector or a matrix. In an abstract vector space this operation is called an inner product.

For two $2\times2$ matrices $M=
  \begin{pmatrix}
    M_{11}&M_{12}\\
    M_{21}&M_{22}
  \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  N=
  \begin{pmatrix}
    N_{11}&N_{12}\\
    N_{21}&N_{22}
  \end{pmatrix},$ the product $C=MN$ has entries $C_{ij}=\sum_k M_{ik}N_{kj}.$ In particular, $\begin{aligned}C_{11}&=M_{11}N_{11}+M_{12}N_{21},\\
  C_{12}&=M_{11}N_{12}+M_{12}N_{22},\\
  C_{21}&=M_{21}N_{11}+M_{22}N_{21},\\
  C_{22}&=M_{21}N_{12}+M_{22}N_{22}.\end{aligned}$ Each entry is a row of the left matrix multiplied by a column of the right matrix. Equivalently, act with $M$ on each column of $N$ and place the resulting columns side by side.

A configuration becomes a column; a one-step law becomes a matrix; repeated time evolution becomes a product of matrices; reversibility becomes the existence of an inverse.
ja: 最初の1時間では、ビットと可逆な矢印を用いて、決定論的な古典物理学を定性的に説明した。残りの数学は、その説明を量子力学への移行に耐えうる形に翻訳する。配置は列になり、1ステップの法則は行列になり、繰り返される時間発展は行列の積になり、可逆性は逆行列の存在になる。
zh: 第一个小时用比特和可逆箭头给出了确定性经典物理的定性描述。余下的数学把这一描述转化为一种能够经受向量子力学过渡的形式。一个构型变成一列；一步定律变成一个矩阵；重复的时间演化变成矩阵的乘积；可逆性变成逆的存在。

p.src: Response: The qualitative problem came first: how should deterministic physics be represented by states and update laws? The algebra is the preparation for the next step. Once qubits are introduced, these manipulations will no longer look detached; they will be the natural language of quantum states and their evolution.
